countedLines.convention: git diff --numstat --no-renames baseline..HEAD over the migration module, catalog and units.json, added lines only, no deletion credit; test leaves and receipts line-exempt but file-counted. Includes this commit's local-stage units.json edit.

migration.name: local_seat_credentials_schema
migration.keyColumn: Closed envelope: json_valid, json_type object, ciphertext/iv/salt/algorithm IS text, ciphertext/iv/salt non-empty, and json_remove of those four members IS {} (no other member, e.g. privateKey or password, can be stored). Base64 shape is not checkable in SQL and is not claimed.
migration.integerColumns: generation and result_generation: typeof integer AND BETWEEN 1 AND 9007199254740991; failed_attempts and locked_until_ms: typeof integer AND BETWEEN 0 AND 9007199254740991 (the catalog guard; numeric text such as 2 is still coerced by affinity).
migration.nullCheckFix: json_type(...) IS 'text' rather than = 'text': json_type returns NULL for a missing path and a CHECK that evaluates to NULL passes, so = would accept a key missing iv or salt (mutants D11/D12 prove the difference).

existingDatabase.method: Byte copies of the existing operator database (read-only source at version 31). C = copy upgraded by the real runner capped at 32; B = copy upgraded to head 33. B minus the two local-seat tables, their unique index and the version-33 record equals C in every sqlite_master entry and every row (migrations compared on version and name, applied_at excluded). A second initialize of B is a no-op; the same code capped at 32 opens B without error or change (cappedRunner), and the REAL older build (a detached worktree at baseline afcbd62bb whose catalog head is 32, not this code with a cap) opens B without error or change (olderBuild, reproducing the reviewer run); dropping the two tables (which drops the index) and the version-33 record (down) restores C exactly and re-applying gives B again. Only counts and hashes are recorded.

migrationReview.suite: The migration suite also proves fresh create, upgrade from head 32, idempotent re-apply after a lost record, rollback of both tables when the record write fails, and the R6 head pin at 33.

carryIn.CF-LSC0-6: Persistence share discharged: no column is named for a password or secret; the key column accepts only the closed ciphertext envelope and fingerprints only a sha256 hex digest (RED rows, mutants D11-D16 and A1-A7). Free-text columns (label, public_key, operation_id) can technically hold any string; the schema cannot prevent that and does not claim to (review L7); the name check is a name check only (review L6). Request-scoped key lifetime and no-secret logging/error/operation-record proof remain LSC-1S/LSC-1.
carryIn.CF-LSC0-8: Persistence share discharged: failed_attempts and locked_until_ms are durable (survive reopen and re-apply; mutants D7/D8) and integer-guarded (review F2; mutants A8-A11). Revoke-keeps and re-provision-clears is repository behaviour routed to LSC-1S.
carryIn.CF-LSC0-16: Persistence share: only the per-seat count and lock deadline persist; the route-wide windows are process-local service state (not stored). Post-expiry counter semantics and window consumption routed to LSC-1S/LSC-1.

firstSweep.note: The first post-fix sweep caught 29/34: A7 (expected equivalent) plus D9, D11, D12 and D13 survived because the new rules masked two existing rows. The F6 unique index rejected the duplicate-operation row before the primary key did (D9), and the now-required algorithm member rejected the iv/salt rows before the NULL-passing member check (D11-D13). Fix in the test leaf only: the iv/salt rows now carry algorithm, and a row reuses an operation id on a different seat and generation. The old-head leg of that first run also failed to compile because the 18319cc5 module copy had been written UTF-16 by a shell redirect; it was regenerated byte-exact and both legs re-run.

postReviewAmendment.equivalentMutants: A7 (drop json_type object) is expected EQUIVALENT: the member IS text clauses already require an object; the clause is kept as the reviewer specified, for readability.
